provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The visible rule does not depend on orientation. Each frame is four 3-cell L brackets of one colour. A bracket's elbow is the cell diagonally opposite the empty cell of its 2x2 box, and the elbow's position in that box tells which corner of the frame it is (TL/TR/BL/BR). A D4 transform maps brackets to brackets and corner roles to corner roles. It may swap wide and tall frames, but 'mirror across the longer dimension' gives the same answer in any orientation. So the emitted program works directly in visible coordinates and needs no rotation or axis constants from d4.

Only the colour roles are specialised: background = palette[0] and marker = palette[1]. Any other colour can be a bracket colour, so the frame colour (palette[2..9]) is detected from pixels.

The program:
1. Erases every marker.
2. Finds the frames. For each TL elbow it takes the nearest TR elbow of the same colour on the same row to the right and the nearest BL elbow in the same column below. It accepts the frame only if a BR elbow sits at the remaining corner. Frame boxes never overlap or touch, so the nearest matching elbow always belongs to the same frame.
3. For each frame, repaints the input markers inside the box. It adds their reflection about the box centre: column reflection (x -> l+r-x) when the box is wider than tall, row reflection (y -> t+b-y) when it is taller than wide.

The approved fixtures follow this uniform rule, with no contradictions.
draft_notes.limitations:
1. Square frames have no defined mirror axis. The constructor never makes them: random scenes are non-square and explicit mode rejects squares. The archived solver falls back to a left-right mirror when w >= h. That tie-break is not D4-invariant and is not part of the visible rule, so it is reported for host review rather than reproduced. This program keeps the markers of a square frame unmirrored.
2. Frames are only recognised if all four elbows are present, which the constructor guarantees. The archived solver does not check the BR corner, so the two could differ only on malformed scenes outside the constructor's domain.
3. The roles background = palette[0] and marker = palette[1] are fixed constants, as the constructor fixes them to 0 and 1.
4. The program does not use the demonstrations.
